attempts.label: CRCNS:rrf-1
attempts.entry_title: Threat and aversive outcome signals in the retrorubral field (Moaddab and McDannald 2021)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's main findings held up in this data: the eight cue-firing clusters at the stated sizes, their danger, uncertainty and safety patterns, and stronger signaling of exaggerated threat probability than of fear output. This rests on the paper's own code, whose normalization differs from its Methods text. The k1 shock response did not reproduce in the 0 to 8 s window drawn in Figure 6, though it did in 0 to 4 s, which fits the supplementary table. Some outcome-period results and the per-cluster regression table held only in part, the latter because the paper leaves out two unnamed units.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Moaddab and McDannald (2021) on CRCNS data set rrf-1, which holds 743 single units recorded from the retrorubral field of 11 rats over 228 fear discrimination sessions, the authors' derived data file, and the paper's MATLAB code. It covers the cue-responsive screen, behavior, the eight k-means clusters, cue firing, the threat probability regressions and the aversive outcome firing of each cluster.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Moaddab and McDannald (2021) from CRCNS rrf-1

outcomes.notes: 743 units, 228 sessions and 11 rats, the paper's three counts. Units per session 1 to 10 (median 3). No unit has the spike train of another and no two sessions share event times, so nothing is deposited twice.

The screen as the code runs it (floored integer rates, a NaN test counted as not significant) gives 423 units from 190 sessions, and the per-rat counts equal Figure S1 exactly (fewest 11, rb11). With unfloored rates from the spike times the same tests select 461 units, 409 of them in common.
deviations: The rates are floored to integer Hz as in cubeScriptPR25.m and rrfAnalysis.m (lines 5 to 60); the Methods do not mention flooring. The unfloored variant is shown.

outcomes.notes: Per rat over the 190 sessions with a cue-responsive unit, cue effect F(2, 20) = 103.57, p = 2.8e-11 (the paper's F and p). Means D 0.871, U 0.449, S 0.051. Differences D-U 0.422 [0.264, 0.516], U-S 0.398 [0.261, 0.748], D-S 0.821 [0.704, 0.891], all excluding zero and within tolerance. Pooling trials per rat gives the same means and CIs that also exclude zero.
deviations: CIs are studentized bootstrap intervals with 1,000 resamples and standard errors s / sqrt(n); MATLAB's bootci, called as in rrfAnalysis.m 1744 with no StdErr, estimates them from 100 nested bootstrap samples (NBootStd). Each CI is judged by the sign it gives in most of 20 draws, a convention of this attempt that the claims file does not set (notebook, bootstrap section); the nested standard errors give the same majority sign for every CI.

outcomes.notes: Under the claims file's reading z-b with scikit-learn's k-means, the criterion is met in all 4 combinations of outcome start (12 or 12.5 s) and runs (best of 10, mean of 10); the outcome rests on these. The other readings of the claims file are mixed, z-b with 10 runs of the MATLAB stream 3 of 4 and z-a 3 of 4 with scikit-learn and 0 of 4 with the MATLAB stream; over the 45 readings in the notebook (three normalizations, three outcome starts, five ways to run k-means) 30 meet it. The code's own runs (rng(1) before each k) meet it with the measure the code plots, mean(sumd) (8224 at k = 1; drops after 8 clusters at most 78.9 against 128.2 from 7 to 8), but that measure is a sum at k = 2, and its drop from 2 to 3 (4848) is larger than from 1 to 2 (1216). With the Methods' measure (mean squared distance per unit) the same runs rise once, from 12 to 13 clusters (by 0.151).
deviations: The k-means matrix is the code's: outcome epochs from 13 s after cue onset (rrfAnalysis.m), not 12 or 12.5 s (the claims file's readings e-a, run as variants). The code runs k-means once per k, not 10 times as the Methods say; the claims file's readings e-b (best of 10, mean of 10 runs) are run as variants, with 10 runs continuing the MATLAB stream after rng(1) (an assumption about how MATLAB draws replicates) and with scikit-learn.

The outcome rests on reading z-b with scikit-learn's k-means++ standing for the Methods' 10 runs (an assumption; with 10 runs of the MATLAB stream z-b meets the criterion in 3 of 4 combinations). The code plots mean(sumd) as a bar plot on a 0 to 9000 axis (rrfAnalysis.m 952 to 986, printed), not the Methods' mean squared distance per unit; mean(sumd) is shown as a variant.

Normalized firing is the code's (cubeScriptPR25.m): single-trial differential rates, floored to integer Hz, z-scored over all 16 trials and all bins of a unit, then averaged by trial type. The Methods (Z-score normalization) describe z-scoring the trial-type means across trial types. The claims file left this open (readings z-a and z-b) and asked an author who finds the code to follow it; z-a and z-b are run as variants. Assumed that the code is what the paper did; the exact recovery of the paper's cluster sizes, F values and correlations under it supports this.

outcomes.notes: The code's run gives clusters of exactly the paper's sizes, and every cluster passes the pattern tests written from Results paragraph 3 (listed in rrf.pattern_checks). Other k-means runs give other partitions: over 50 scikit-learn seeds, single runs show all eight patterns 16% of the time and best-of-10 runs 46%, with a median of 3 sizes within 10%, and none gives all eight patterns with all eight sizes within 10%. No reading of the claims file gives all eight sizes within 10%: over outcome starts 12, 12.5 and 13 s, normalizations code, z-a and z-b, the code's single run and the best of 10 runs of the MATLAB stream, only the code's own combination does (others at most 4 of 8); of the 10 runs of the stream with the code's matrix, one gives the paper's sizes and patterns.

findings.statement: The Methods (Z-score normalization) describe averaging trials per trial type, subtracting that type's 2-s baseline and z-scoring the means across trial types. The paper's code (cubeScriptPR25.m, in the data set) instead floors every rate to an integer Hz, subtracts each trial's own 2-s baseline, and z-scores the single-trial values over all 16 trials and all bins of a unit; the trial-type means of these are what rrfAnalysis.m analyses. The paper's numbers (cluster sizes, Table 1, Table S1, Figure 4 and Figure 5 statistics) are reproduced to the printed digits only with the code's version. Question for the authors: is the code's normalization the one used for all reported results?

The Methods say k-means clustering was performed 10 times for each cluster number and that Figure 1E shows the mean squared distance between each point and its centroid. rrfAnalysis.m runs kmeans once per cluster number after rng(1), and plots mean(sumd), the mean over clusters of the summed squared distances (sum(sumd) for two clusters). The outcome epochs of the clustering matrix start 13 s after cue onset, 0.5 s after shock offset, which the Methods do not state.

For k1, k3, k5 and k6 the gray boxes of Figure 6 span 0 to 8 s after shock offset, but the Table S4 means of these clusters are reproduced (to within 0.008) only by the window 0 to 4 s after shock offset; in 0 to 8 s they differ by up to 0.15. The 17.5-s windows of the other four clusters reproduce Table S4 exactly. The paper's code does not draw the boxes; its traces put 0 s at shock offset, and its own post-shock windows are 0 to 2 s and 7.5 to 17.5 s (rrfAnalysis.m 6097, 6135).

Question for the authors: which interval after shock offset was analysed in Figure 6 (columns i and ii) and Table S4 for k1, k3, k5 and k6? The figure's gray boxes show 0 to 8 s; the table's values fit 0 to 4 s. The answer decides fig6a-k1-shock, which is not reproduced in 0 to 8 s and is in 0 to 4 s, and the k5 omission mean of fig6de.

The ANOVAs of Figure 5E and Table S3 have 355 error df, implying 362 units, while the seven clusters hold 364. Removing one k3 unit (four candidates fit equally) and one k5 unit reproduces Table S3's F and p values for those clusters, and Table S3's partial eta squared for k3 fits 17 units; the pooled ANOVA without two such units gives F values near the paper's but not equal. The paper does not say which units were left out or why. Question for the authors: which two units were excluded from these ANOVAs, and on what rule?

The data set holds no cluster labels and no per-unit electrode location. The labels can be recovered only by re-running the code's k-means (rng(1); kmeans in MATLAB) and its hand-written map from cluster numbers to k1..k8; the bregma level is a per-rat table inside rrfAnalysis.m. The event channels (EVT01 shock, EVT09/11/12 cues by program letter, EVT13 nose poke, EVT14 pause recording) are named only in comments of cubeScriptPR25.m; EVT08, listed there as empty, repeats EVT01 in every file.

The unit files hold spikes only from 20 s before to about 33.5 s after each cue onset: recording was paused between trials (EVT14 comes 31.5 to 33.5 s after each cue onset). The data descriptor does not say so; a user who computes rates over the inter-trial interval would read the gaps as silence.

The data descriptor says RRFcube.wave holds a mean waveform for each trial type (it holds one 32-sample waveform per unit), that poke.base is the nose poke rate 2 s before the cue (it is the rate over 20 s, as the code computes it), and lists half-duration and amplitude-ratio fields that cube.mat does not contain (rrfAnalysis.m computes them from the waveform).
The paper and descriptor give a mean inter-trial interval of 3.5 min; cue onsets in the data are 203 to 265 s apart (mean 3.89 min), which includes the 10-s cue and the trial period.

entries.name: crcns-rrf-1-moaddab-2021
entries.title: Threat and aversive outcome signals in the retrorubral field (Moaddab and McDannald 2021)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Moaddab and McDannald (2021) on CRCNS data set rrf-1, which holds 743 single units recorded from the retrorubral field of 11 rats over 228 fear discrimination sessions, the authors' derived data file, and the paper's MATLAB code. It covers the cue-responsive screen, behavior, the eight k-means clusters, cue firing, the threat probability regressions and the aversive outcome firing of each cluster.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Moaddab and McDannald (2021) from CRCNS rrf-1
